title: Point at the broken case
kicker: World 6 · Prove It & Fix It · Level 2

job.text: The case-set runner shows 1 of 4 cases red: February expected 980 but got 1,120. Re-direct the build to fix it — without hard-coding February and without loosening the check to make it pass. All four cases must still be green after. In your own words you would point at the failing case and ask for a root fix; here you build that ask from the checklist.

preview.more: seed-42 sales · 1 of 4 red (February counts a refund as a sale)

text.plain: Tell me which case is red and what it expected versus what it got, before changing anything.
text.tech: Report the failing case: its id, expected value, and actual value, before editing.

text.plain: After the fix, re-run all four cases — every one that was green must stay green.
text.tech: After the fix, execute the full case set and assert no previously-green case regressed.

text.plain: Let the AI talk you through why it's fixed instead of re-running the cases.
text.tech: Accept the model's prose explanation of the fix in place of re-running the cases.

text.plain: Just remind it to be thorough so it gets February right.
text.tech: Just remind it to be thorough on the failing month.

subChoiceGroup: How should it fix the failing case?

subChoices.label: Fix the underlying rule (handle refunds for every month)
Loosen the check so February passes as-is

rules.claim: 4 of 4 green after the fix. The check is unchanged.
rules.feedback: Fixed at the root. You found the real reason February failed — a refund counted as a sale — fixed the rule for every month, re-ran all four, and nothing else broke. That's a fix, not a patch.
rules.lesson: Localize, fix the rule, keep the check.

output.source: the rule fixed at the root, check intact, no regression

rules.claim: February passes now, but March came back red.
rules.feedback: You fixed the case, not the rule. Hard-coding February to 980 made February green and broke March. Point at why February failed and fix the rule behind it, not the one month.

output.source: an overfit: if month == Feb return 980

rules.claim: All four green — because the check now asks for less.
rules.feedback: You passed it by lowering the bar. The cases are green because the check now accepts a wider range, not because the tool got right. Don't trade the check away for a green — fix the tool.
rules.lesson: Don't trade the check away for a green.

output.source: a check weakened until the wrong answer fits

rules.claim: "Just fix it." — February still red, or fixed by guesswork.
rules.feedback: "Just fix it" doesn't say what to fix. You didn't localize the failure or demand the whole set re-run, so you can't tell a real fix from an overfit. Point at the broken case, fix the rule, and re-run all four.
rules.lesson: A vague fix hides whether anything actually got better.

hints.nudge: Which case is red, and what did it expect versus get?
hints.gap: Watch the trap: hard-coding February breaks March, and loosening the check only hides the error. The case isn't the problem — the rule is. February counts a refund as a sale.
hints.moves: Add Localize the failure and Re-run all cases, no regressions, and choose Fix the underlying rule — not special-casing February and not loosening the check.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "just fix it" → an overfit that passes February and breaks March.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: localize the failing case, fix the rule behind it, re-run all four → clean, no regression, check intact.

template.plain: Case [X] failed: it expected [E] but got [G]. Fix the underlying rule so it passes — don't special-case [X] — and re-run ALL cases to prove nothing else broke.
template.tech: Case [X] failed (expected [E], got [G]). Fix the root rule, do not hard-code [X], and re-run the whole case set to prove no regression.

notes: ChatGPT: demand it show all cases green after the fix, not just the one that failed.
Copilot in Excel: re-check every test row, not only the one you fixed.
A chat AI that can't run code: re-run the whole case set yourself; an overfit shows up as a new red elsewhere. Never accept "I fixed it" without seeing every case.
